main.note: Verbatim local text with whitespace normalized. Lesson analysis is interpretation, not part of this quotation.

narrativeBlocks.title: The scene
narrativeBlocks.body: Frazer discusses Pausanias’ familiarity with Mount Sipylus, including monuments linked with Tantalus, Pelops, and Niobe. Here Frazer is describing an ancient writer’s observations; the paragraph is not Frazer’s own eyewitness confirmation of those heroes.

narrativeBlocks.title: What the source does
narrativeBlocks.body: Source quotation (translation; whitespace normalized): “wheeling above the lonely tarn of Tantalus in the heart of the hills; he had beheld the stately tomb of the same hero on Mount Sipylus, the ruined city at the bottom of the clear lake, the rock-hewn throne of Pelops crowning the dizzy peak that overhangs the cañon, and the dripping rock which popular”

narrativeBlocks.title: Why it matters
narrativeBlocks.body: Interpretation: places can preserve stories without proving their events. Frazer’s dated scholarship must be checked against the ancient testimony he discusses.

narrativeBlocks.title: Read it carefully
narrativeBlocks.body: Identify each layer of testimony: a legendary association, Pausanias’ description, and Frazer’s discussion of it. None should be silently promoted into direct proof that a legendary event occurred.

narrativeBlocks.title: Carry it forward
narrativeBlocks.body: Landscape gives heroic afterlife a physical address.

quiz.prompt: Whose observations is Frazer discussing in this passage?
quiz.explanation: Pausanias’. Revisit the named passage and distinguish its narrative from the lesson’s interpretation.

quiz.prompt: What does a named legendary tomb establish by itself?

choices.text: The historical truth of every attached episode
An association between a place and a story, not proof the hero lived there
